contracts.name: Alert
contracts.summary: A persistent message inside the page that explains a state or problem and stays until the cause is gone or the user dismisses it.
useWhen: A message that must stay visible while the user works: a failed publish, validation summary, locked entry, missing permission.
A problem the user has to fix or a state they need to know about before acting (e.g. "This entry is scheduled; edits go live at 18:00").
System-wide notices across the top of the app (maintenance, expiring licence): use --banner.
Short inline hints under a field or in a form section: use --compact.

dontUseWhen.case: A short confirmation that something just worked ("Article published")
A question the user must answer before continuing
An error tied to a single form field
dontUseWhen.use: input with gds-input--error and its helper text

dontUseWhen.case: A status label on a row or card

anatomy.description: Wrapper. Flex row: icon, body, close. Base styles are the info colours.

attributes.role: "alert" for errors, "status" for others, only when the alert is inserted after a user action (see rules). No role when it is part of the page on load.

anatomy.description: Icon slot (24px, 16px in --compact). Holds a Lucide icon that matches the variant. Coloured by the variant.
Column that holds content, link and actions. Takes the remaining width.
Stacks title and description.
Short headline (14px medium). Use a heading tag when the alert starts a section of the page.
Explanation (14px regular). Use title, description or both; one of them is needed.
Text link below the content ("Read more", "View errors"). Use <button type="button"> when it does not navigate.
Trailing icon in the link (16px), e.g. external-link or arrow-right.
Row of buttons (gds-btn --sm) below the content.
Dismiss button (32px), last child of the alert. Contains a Lucide x icon.
Time bar at the bottom of a --toast alert. Width set by product JS. Needs position: relative on the alert (known issue).

modifiers.description: Purple. Neutral information.
Green. Something worked or is ready.
Orange. Something needs attention soon.
Red. Something failed or is blocked.
Description only, smaller padding (12px), items centred. Leave out the title.
Smallest form for inline hints: 8/12px padding, 16px icon, 12px text.
4px coloured left border in the variant colour.
Full width, no radius, no left/right border. For the top of the app or a page.
Floating card: white background, shadow, max 400px, slide-in animation, coloured left border per variant. For rich notifications with title and actions.
Fades and slides out. Add with JS, then remove the element after the transition.

states.name: dismissing
states.how: Add gds-alert--dismissing, wait for the transition (normal duration), then remove the element and move focus to a sensible place if the close button had focus.

a11y: Live role only for alerts added after a user action: role="alert" (assertive) for errors, role="status" (polite) for the rest. A live region must not be on alerts that are present on page load.
Icon is decorative (aria-hidden="true"); the title or description says what happened. Colour is never the only signal.
__close is a <button type="button"> with an aria-label. After dismiss, move focus to the next logical element (product JS).
Do not auto-hide an inline alert. Only --toast alerts may time out, and they pause on hover and focus (product JS).
In --compact the close button shrinks to 16px, below the 24px minimum target: do not use __close there.

rules.rule: An alert inserted after a user action has role="alert" (error) or role="status" (info, success, warning). An alert present on page load has no live role.
rules.why: Screen readers announce new messages only through a live role; a role on static content makes them announce it on every load.

rules.rule: .gds-alert__close is a <button type="button"> with an aria-label.
rules.why: The button shows only an x icon, so it has no name without aria-label.

rules.rule: .gds-alert__icon has aria-hidden="true" and the alert has a __title or __desc with text.
rules.why: The meaning lives in the text, not in the icon or colour.

rules.rule: An alert has exactly one variant (--info, --success, --warning, --error). Write --info explicitly even though it is the default look.
rules.why: Two variants give an undefined colour; an explicit class makes intent readable.

rules.rule: Icons: info → info, success → check, warning → alert-triangle, error → alert-circle.
rules.why: Same icon for the same meaning everywhere, as in the docs.

rules.rule: Short "it worked" confirmations use gds-toast, not an inline alert or gds-alert--toast.
rules.why: Alerts are for messages that must stay; a confirmation that stays clutters the page.
rules.removeInV3: Merge gds-alert--toast and gds-toast into one toast component so there is only one choice.

rules.rule: .gds-alert__progress is used only inside a .gds-alert--toast, which needs position: relative (inline style or the toast container).
rules.why: The bar is absolutely positioned; without a positioned alert it sticks to another element.
rules.removeInV3: Give .gds-alert--toast position: relative in the CSS.

rules.rule: Do not put .gds-alert__close inside a .gds-alert--compact.
rules.why: Compact shrinks the button to 16px, below the 24px minimum target size.
rules.removeInV3: Keep the close button at 24px or more in compact.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-alert__progress is position: absolute but .gds-alert has no position: relative (only inside .gds-toast-container). Docs add style="position:relative" by hand.
knownIssues.fix: Add position: relative to .gds-alert--toast.

knownIssues.issue: Two toast implementations: .gds-alert--toast (400px, title, actions, progress bar) and .gds-toast (490px, single line, timer ring), with different shadows and radii.
knownIssues.fix: v3: one toast component with an optional title/actions slot.

knownIssues.issue: Naming: alert uses --error while toast, badge and button use --critical.
knownIssues.fix: v3: rename to --critical (keep --error as an alias for one release).

knownIssues.issue: Alert info is purple while badge --info is blue.
knownIssues.fix: Decide one info colour for all components.

knownIssues.issue: --compact sets __close to 16×16px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px target size.
knownIssues.fix: Keep a 24px hit area (padding or min-size) in compact.

knownIssues.issue: __link is inline-flex; inside __desc the docs need style="display:inline".
knownIssues.fix: Add an inline link variant, or make the link display: inline when inside __desc.

knownIssues.issue: __close focus ring borrows --input-focus-* tokens.
knownIssues.fix: Use a shared focus-ring token.

knownIssues.issue: Docs side panel example uses old alert markup (class on <i>, no __body).
knownIssues.fix: Update the docs example to the anatomy here.

contracts.name: Avatar
contracts.summary: A photo, initials or icon that represents a person or an organisation, alone, stacked in a group or paired with a name.
useWhen: Showing who wrote, edited or owns an entry or asset.
Listing collaborators on an item (avatar group).
A user or author cell in a table, paired with the name (avatar name).
Representing an organisation, site or publication (square shape).

dontUseWhen.case: A removable person token in a field or filter
A presence indicator without a picture
A thumbnail of an image or video asset
dontUseWhen.use: a plain in a card or table cell

anatomy.description: Overlapping stack of avatars. Uses row-reverse: the first child in the DOM appears on the right, in front.
"+N" for people not shown. Must be the FIRST child of the group so it appears last (on the right). Fixed at 32px.
Avatar + name pair. Contains one .gds-avatar followed by .gds-avatar-name__info.
The avatar circle or square. 32px circle by default. Contains exactly one of __img, __text or __icon, plus an optional __status. Can sit alone, in .gds-avatar-group, in .gds-avatar-name or in a chip.

attributes.role: "img" when it shows initials or an icon and no name is visible next to it
attributes.aria-label: The full name of the person or organisation

anatomy.description: Photo or logo, cropped to fill.

attributes.alt: Required. The name when the avatar stands alone; alt="" when the name is visible next to it

anatomy.description: Initials (one or two letters). Shown in upper case.

attributes.aria-hidden: "true"; the name comes from the avatar's aria-label or the visible name

anatomy.description: Fallback icon when there is no photo or name: for people, "building-2" for organisations. Size follows the avatar size.
Small green "online" dot in the bottom-right corner, with a white ring. Only one colour exists.
Text column next to the avatar.
The name. Truncates with an ellipsis.
Second line: role, email or team. Truncates with an ellipsis.

modifiers.description: 16px. Inline in text or very dense lists.
20px.
24px. Table cells and compact lists.
32px. Same as the base size.
40px. Comments, cards, panel headers.
48px.
64px. Profile headers.
Round. For people. Same as the base shape.
Rounded square. For organisations, sites and publications.
Smaller name and subtitle text. Pair with a 32px avatar.
Smallest text (both lines the same size). Pair with a 24px avatar.
Muted name and subtitle colours, for secondary mentions.

a11y: Every .gds-avatar__img has alt. Use alt="" when the name is already visible next to it (avatar name, table cell), so it is not read twice.
An initials or icon avatar with no visible name gets role="img" and aria-label with the full name; initials alone mean nothing to a screen reader.
Status is not shown by colour alone: give .gds-avatar__status role="img" and aria-label="Online", or say it in text nearby.
In a group, each avatar needs a name (alt or aria-label) and the group an aria-label with the total count.
The group's DOM order is the reverse of what people see; keep groups non-interactive or see knownIssues.

rules.rule: Every .gds-avatar__img has an alt attribute (empty when the name is visible next to it).
rules.why: Without alt, screen readers read the file name.

rules.rule: An avatar with initials or an icon and no visible name next to it has role="img" and aria-label with the full name.
rules.why: "FK" or a generic person icon does not tell anyone who it is.

rules.rule: .gds-avatar__status has role="img" and aria-label, or the status is written in nearby text.
rules.why: A green dot is colour only. aria-label on a plain span is ignored, so it needs the img role.

rules.rule: Circle for people, square for organisations, sites and publications.
rules.why: The shape tells people at a glance whether it is a person or an entity.

rules.rule: .gds-avatar__text holds one or two letters.
rules.why: More letters do not fit the circle at small sizes.

rules.rule: .gds-avatar-group__counter is the first child of .gds-avatar-group.
rules.why: The group uses row-reverse, so the first child appears last; anywhere else the counter lands in the middle of the stack.
rules.removeInV3: Use normal row order with z-index stacking so the counter goes last, where people expect it.

rules.rule: All avatars in a .gds-avatar-group use the same size.
rules.why: The overlap and the counter are tuned for one size; mixed sizes look broken.

rules.rule: To show an avatar with a name, use .gds-avatar-name, not a custom flex row.
rules.why: It already handles spacing, truncation and type sizes.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-avatar-group uses flex-direction: row-reverse, so screen readers and keyboard focus go through the avatars in the opposite order to what people see, and the counter must come first in the DOM.
knownIssues.fix: v3: normal order, negative margin-left and z-index stacking.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-avatar-group__counter is fixed at 32px. Docs patch other sizes with inline styles, and gds-avatar--24 on the counter loses to the counter rule.
knownIssues.fix: Add group size modifiers (e.g. gds-avatar-group--24) that size both the avatars and the counter.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-avatar__status is always green (online) and duplicates status-dot, which has busy, away and offline.
knownIssues.fix: Allow a .gds-status-dot--ring inside .gds-avatar in the status position, and deprecate __status.

knownIssues.issue: gds-avatar-name--soft subtitle (neutral-80 on white) is about 3:1, below the 4.5:1 needed for small text.
knownIssues.fix: Use neutral-300 or the text-secondary token for the soft subtitle.

knownIssues.issue: At 16px, the icon size token is also 16px, so the fallback icon fills the whole avatar with no padding.
knownIssues.fix: Set --avatar-icon-16 to 10–12px.

contracts.name: Badge
contracts.summary: A small label that shows the status or category of something.
useWhen: Showing a status in a table cell or card (Published, Draft…).
Labelling a category or count next to an item.

dontUseWhen.case: Something people can click to filter or remove
A percentage change

anatomy.description: Wrapper.
Coloured dot. Use for statuses.
Icon slot (Lucide, 12px), instead of the dot.
The text.
Number after the label.

modifiers.description: Gray.
Green.
Orange.
Red.
Blue.
Purple. Categories only, no status meaning.
Outlined instead of filled.
Strong solid fill, for high emphasis.
Text only, no background.
Small.
Medium.
Large.

a11y: Never show status by colour alone: always include .gds-badge__label text.
The dot and icon are decorative; the label carries the meaning.

rules.rule: Content status mapping: Published → positive, Draft → neutral, Scheduled → warning, Archived → neutral, Edited → info, Unpublished → neutral, Deleted → critical.
rules.why: Design decisions (11 and 13 Nov 2026). Scheduled changes state on its own and Edited has unpublished changes, so both draw attention; Draft, Archived and Unpublished need no action; Deleted is a loss.

rules.rule: Status badges use the dot + label form.
rules.why: Status is not shown by colour alone.

rules.rule: A badge has exactly one colour variant.
rules.why: Two variants on one badge produce an undefined colour.

rules.rule: A badge is never a button or link.
rules.why: Badges have no hover or focus styles.

knownIssues.issue: Without a variant class the badge has no defined colour.
knownIssues.fix: v3: neutral by default, so the variant becomes optional.

contracts.name: Button
contracts.summary: Triggers an action: text buttons, icon-only buttons and joined button groups.
useWhen: Running an action on the current page: Save, Publish, Delete, Create entry.
Opening a dialog, menu or panel.
An icon-only action in a dense toolbar or table row, when the icon is widely understood (more, close, edit).

dontUseWhen.case: Going to another page or URL
dontUseWhen.use: a link (<a href>); if it must look like a button, put .gds-btn on the <a>

dontUseWhen.case: Switching a setting on or off
Filtering a list by one or more values
Choosing between views inside one panel

anatomy.description: Joins adjacent .gds-btn elements into one bar with shared borders. Only direct .gds-btn children are joined.

attributes.aria-label: What the buttons control, e.g. "Date range"

anatomy.description: Text button. Needs one size and one variant modifier: the base class has no height, padding or colour. Can sit alone or inside .gds-btn-group.

attributes.href: Required when the element is an <a>

anatomy.description: Loading spinner: . Only with gds-btn--loading. Centred over the hidden label.
Icon slot before or after the label. Wraps one Lucide icon; the size modifier sets the icon size. Decorative: the label carries the meaning.
The button text. Loading hides only this element, so all text must be inside it.
Square icon-only button, used instead of .gds-btn. Contains one Lucide icon directly (no __icon wrapper). Needs one size and one variant modifier.

modifiers.description: Filled brand colour. The main action of a view.
White with a border. Supporting actions.
No background or border until hover. Low-emphasis actions in toolbars and cards.
Red fill. Destructive actions (delete, remove, revoke).
Green fill. Confirming a positive outcome (approve, mark as done).
24px high, 12px icon.
28px high, 14px icon. Toolbars, table rows, cards.
36px high, 16px icon. Forms, page headers, dialogs.
44px high, 18px icon.
52px high, 20px icon. Landing or onboarding screens only.
Fully rounded corners.
Takes the full width of its container.
Hides the label (keeps the width) and shows .gds-btn__spinner. Add aria-busy="true". Does not block clicks on its own.
Disabled look for elements that cannot take the disabled attribute (<a>). On <button>, use the disabled attribute instead.
Filled brand colour.
White with a border.
Transparent until hover. The usual choice in toolbars, table rows and dialog headers.
Red fill. Destructive actions.
Green fill.
24px square, 12px icon.
28px square, 14px icon.
36px square, 16px icon.
44px square, 18px icon.
52px square, 20px icon.
Round instead of square.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover. Skipped when the button is disabled.

states.name: active
states.how: Native :active: darker fill and a slight press (scale).

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible shows a two-ring focus outline.

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled attribute on <button>. On <a>: gds-btn--disabled + aria-disabled="true" + remove href. .gds-btn-icon supports the attribute only.

states.name: loading
states.how: gds-btn--loading + .gds-btn__spinner + aria-busy="true". Ignore clicks in JS while loading.

a11y: Use <button> for actions and <a href> for navigation, whatever it looks like.
Every .gds-btn-icon needs an aria-label that names the action.
Use the native disabled attribute on <button>; the class alone leaves it clickable and focusable.
While loading, keep the label in the DOM (it stays the accessible name) and set aria-busy="true".
Give .gds-btn-group role="group" and an aria-label. If the group works as a toggle, set aria-pressed on each button.

rules.rule: Every .gds-btn and .gds-btn-icon has exactly one size and one variant modifier.
rules.why: The base class has no height, padding or colours, so a bare button renders as an unstyled box.
rules.removeInV3: Make md + secondary the built-in default so both modifiers become optional.

rules.rule: Every .gds-btn-icon has an aria-label (or aria-labelledby).
rules.why: An icon alone has no text, so screen readers announce just "button".

rules.rule: All text inside .gds-btn sits in .gds-btn__label; icons sit in .gds-btn__icon.
rules.why: Loading hides only the label element, and the icon size comes from the __icon wrapper.

rules.rule: A disabled <button> uses the disabled attribute. gds-btn--disabled is only for <a>, together with aria-disabled="true".
rules.why: The class only changes the look; the button would still be focusable and clickable.
rules.removeInV3: Drop gds-btn--disabled and style only :disabled and [aria-disabled="true"].

rules.rule: A gds-btn--loading button has aria-busy="true" and contains .gds-btn__spinner.
rules.why: Without aria-busy, screen-reader users get no sign that something is happening; without the spinner the button just looks empty.

rules.rule: A <button class="gds-btn"> or <button class="gds-btn-icon"> inside a form has type="button" unless it submits the form.
rules.why: A button in a form submits it by default, which surprises people when the button only opens a menu.

rules.rule: At most one gds-btn--primary per view or dialog.
rules.why: One clear main action; two primaries compete and slow the decision.

rules.rule: Use gds-btn--critical only for actions that delete or remove something, and gds-btn--positive only to confirm a good outcome.
rules.why: Red and green carry meaning; using them for emphasis teaches people to ignore them.

rules.rule: Navigation uses <a href class="gds-btn ...">; actions use <button>.
rules.why: Links and buttons behave differently for keyboards, new tabs and screen readers.

rules.rule: A .gds-btn-group contains only .gds-btn elements of one size.
rules.why: The group only joins direct .gds-btn children and sets corner radius per size; icon buttons or mixed sizes break the joined edges.
rules.removeInV3: Support .gds-btn-icon in groups and take the radius from the group, not each child.

knownIssues.issue: Docs use gds-btn--icon-left, gds-btn--icon-right and gds-btn--icon-only, and the SCSS header lists --icon-left/--icon-right, but none of these classes exist in the CSS.
knownIssues.fix: Remove them from docs and the header comment. The gap already spaces icon and label; icon-only buttons use .gds-btn-icon.

knownIssues.issue: A bare .gds-btn or .gds-btn-icon has no size and no colours. brand.md says md is the default and shows buttons without a size class, which is wrong.
knownIssues.fix: v3: make md + secondary the default. Until then, fix brand.md.

knownIssues.issue: gds-btn--loading does not block clicks or hover, and a .gds-btn__icon stays visible next to the spinner.
knownIssues.fix: Add pointer-events: none and hide .gds-btn__icon while loading.

knownIssues.issue: On secondary and ghost, the loading colour (neutral-60) makes the spinner about 2.1:1 against white, below the 3:1 needed for non-text graphics.
knownIssues.fix: Use --gds-color-text-secondary for the spinner on light buttons.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-btn-icon has no disabled class and its variant hovers only check :disabled, so an <a class="gds-btn-icon"> cannot look disabled.
knownIssues.fix: Add [aria-disabled="true"] styling shared by both button types.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-btn-group only styles direct .gds-btn children; a .gds-btn-icon inside keeps its own radius and doubles borders.
knownIssues.fix: Extend the group selectors to .gds-btn-icon.

knownIssues.issue: There is no selected style for a button inside .gds-btn-group, yet docs show Day/Week/Month groups that read as a toggle.
knownIssues.fix: Add a pressed style driven by aria-pressed="true", or point toggles to tabs.

knownIssues.issue: Docs token table lists --btn-critical-bg as red-600; the SCSS uses red-700.
knownIssues.fix: Regenerate the docs token table from the SCSS.

contracts.name: Calendar / Date picker
contracts.summary: A month grid for picking a date (and optionally a time), shown inline or in a popover under a date field.
useWhen: Picking one date where the weekday or nearby dates matter (publish date, embargo date, report day).
Picking a date and time together (scheduled publish).
Offering product-defined shortcuts next to the grid (advanced layout with presets: "30 days from first upload").

dontUseWhen.case: A date people know by heart and type faster (date of birth)
dontUseWhen.use: input with a date format hint

dontUseWhen.case: A relative period for a report (Last 7 days, This month)
Showing scheduled content over weeks or months
dontUseWhen.use: a dedicated schedule view, not the picker grid

anatomy.description: Wrapper for the CSS-only date picker: position: relative anchor for .gds-calendar-popover, full width. Holds a .gds-input trigger and the popover. Not used when the ds-core createDatePicker() renders the picker (it portals a .gds-popover instead).
Floating surface under the trigger (bottom-start, absolute). Hidden until --open. The product toggles it and handles collisions.

attributes.id: Referenced by aria-controls on the trigger

anatomy.description: The calendar body: header → grid → time → footer in a column. Can sit in .gds-calendar-popover, in a .gds-popover, or inline on the page.
Advanced layout only: left column that holds header, grid, time and footer next to __presets.
Row: previous button, title, next button. Present in date and date-time modes; left out in time-only mode.
Previous / next month. Put it on a .gds-btn-icon gds-btn-icon--ghost gds-btn-icon--sm with a chevron-left / chevron-right icon.
Month and year, e.g. "November 2026". Plain text, or __title-select + __title-year.
Month picker affordance ("June" + chevron). Looks like a select; the behaviour is the product's.
Year next to __title-select.
Carries role="grid" so the weekday row and the day rows are valid grid children. display: contents, so it does not affect layout. Required whenever the month grid is shown.
Weekday header row, 7 columns.
Short weekday name (uppercase). 7 of them, in the locale's week order.

attributes.aria-label: Full weekday name when the text is abbreviated

anatomy.description: 7 × 6 grid of days. Always reserves 6 rows so the popover does not jump between months.
One week (6 per month). display: contents, so the days stay direct grid items.
One day: the day number. 7 per week; adjacent-month days fill the first and last weeks with --outside.

attributes.tabindex: 0 on exactly one day (selected, else focused / first enabled), -1 on the rest

anatomy.description: Small dot under the number: the day has events (e.g. scheduled articles). Decorative; say it in the day's aria-label too.
Time row under the grid (date-time and time-only modes), with a divider on top.
"Time" label before the stepper (date-time mode).
HH : MM control: two __unit segments and a __separator.
Bordered segment: number field + spin column. Shows the focus colour on its border when the field is focused.
Two-digit hour or minute. Arrow Up / Down step the value (product or ds-core JS).
Column with the up and down buttons.
Up (first, with --up) or down (second) step button with a chevron icon.
The ":" between hours and minutes.
Bottom row with .gds-btn gds-btn--ghost gds-btn--sm actions (Today / Now, Clear, Apply). Ghost buttons here are recoloured to the action colour.
Advanced layout only: right column with __presets-title and a .gds-menu of shortcuts. Stacks under the calendar below 640px.
Title of the presets column.

modifiers.description: Shows the popover (fade + slide). Set aria-expanded="true" on the trigger.
Aligns the popover to the end edge of the trigger instead of the start.
Smaller day cells (re-points --calendar-day-size).
Two columns: __main (calendar) and __presets. Needs both children.
Day from the previous / next month. Muted colour.
Today: inset ring + medium weight (not colour only). Add aria-current="date".
Selected day: action-colour fill. Add aria-selected="true".
Day between range start and end: tinted band that bridges the grid gap.
First day of a range: filled disc, band reaches inward.
Last day of a range: filled disc, band reaches inward.
Unavailable day (before min, after max, blocked). Wins over every other state. Also set disabled and aria-disabled="true".
No divider and no top padding: for a time-only panel.
The up button: adds the divider line under it. The down button has no modifier.

states.name: open
states.how: gds-calendar-popover--open on the popover + aria-expanded="true" on the trigger (or the ds-core controller adds gds-popover--open).

states.name: selected
states.how: gds-calendar__day--selected + aria-selected="true" + tabindex="0".

states.name: today
states.how: gds-calendar__day--today + aria-current="date".

states.name: disabled day
states.how: gds-calendar__day--disabled + disabled + aria-disabled="true".

states.name: range
states.how: --range-start, --in-range and --range-end on the days of the range (no ds-core support yet).

states.name: focused day
states.how: Native :focus ring on the day that has tabindex="0"; arrow keys move it (JS).

a11y: Grid structure: __grid-wrap role="grid" (aria-label = month) > __weekdays role="row" > __weekday role="columnheader", and __grid role="rowgroup" > __week role="row" > __day role="gridcell".
Days are <button>s with a full-date aria-label. Exactly one day has tabindex="0" (roving tabindex); arrow keys move by day / week, Page Up / Down by month (JS).
Selected: aria-selected="true". Today: aria-current="date". Disabled: disabled + aria-disabled="true".
Prev / next buttons need aria-label. Announce month changes in a visually hidden aria-live="polite" region (.gds-sr-only).
The popover is role="dialog" with an aria-label; the trigger field gets role="combobox", aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded and aria-controls. Escape closes and focus returns to the field.
Today is shown with a ring + bold number, not colour alone. Forced-colours mode maps states to system colours.
Time fields are role="spinbutton" with aria-valuemin / max / now and an aria-label.

rules.rule: Wrap weekdays and weeks in __grid-wrap role="grid"; every __day sits in a __week role="row" inside __grid role="rowgroup".
rules.why: Gridcells outside a row are invalid ARIA, so screen readers lose row and column position. The static docs previews get this wrong; the ds-core output gets it right.

rules.rule: .gds-calendar__day is a <button type="button"> with role="gridcell" and a full-date aria-label.
rules.why: A bare number like "18" says nothing to a screen reader; a button is focusable and clickable.

rules.rule: --selected has aria-selected="true", --today has aria-current="date", --disabled has disabled and aria-disabled="true".
rules.why: The class only changes the look; the attribute is what assistive tech reads.
rules.removeInV3: Style the days from the ARIA attributes ([aria-selected], [aria-current], [aria-disabled]) so the class and the attribute cannot drift apart.

rules.rule: Exactly one __day has tabindex="0"; all others have tabindex="-1".
rules.why: Tab should enter the grid once and leave it; 42 tab stops make the form unusable by keyboard.

rules.rule: Each __nav button has an aria-label ("Previous month" / "Next month").
rules.why: They are icon-only buttons.

rules.rule: Build parts from existing components: __nav on .gds-btn-icon (ghost, sm), footer actions as .gds-btn--ghost --sm, the trigger as .gds-input, presets as .gds-menu.
rules.why: The calendar CSS only adds layout; colours, focus and sizes come from those components.

rules.rule: When a day has __day-dot, add what it means to the day's aria-label (e.g. ", 2 articles scheduled").
rules.why: The dot is a visual cue only.

rules.rule: Always render 6 full weeks (42 days); fill before and after the month with --outside days.
rules.why: Keeps the 7-column grid aligned and the popover height stable when paging months; matches ds-core.

rules.rule: For a working picker use createDatePicker() from @gjirafa/ds-core instead of writing open/close, keyboard and date logic again.
rules.why: The CSS ships no behaviour; ds-core already handles keyboard, ARIA, positioning and locale.

rules.rule: Use one floating surface per picker: .gds-calendar-popover (CSS only) or .gds-popover (ds-core), never both.
rules.why: Both draw a border, shadow and radius; nesting them doubles the frame.
rules.removeInV3: Rebuild .gds-calendar-popover on .gds-popover (planned in the popover docs) and remove it.

knownIssues.issue: Fails principle 1 (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8 target size): the time stepper up/down buttons are about 16×16px; the minimum is 24×24px (axe).
knownIssues.fix: Give .gds-time-stepper buttons a 24px minimum hit area (padding or min-width/min-height), keeping the 16px icon.

knownIssues.issue: Two popover surfaces exist: .gds-calendar-popover (absolute, inside .gds-datepicker) and the generic .gds-popover that the ds-core date picker actually renders. Same look, two code paths.
knownIssues.fix: Make .gds-calendar-popover compose .gds-popover (already planned in the popover docs), then deprecate it and .gds-datepicker.

knownIssues.issue: ds-core createDatePicker() renders classes that are not in the CSS: gds-datepicker__popover and gds-time-stepper__btn--down.
knownIssues.fix: Remove them from ds-core, or add them to the CSS and this contract.

knownIssues.issue: The static docs previews put role="grid" on __grid with gridcells as direct children (no __grid-wrap, no __week rows) and the weekday row outside the grid. That is invalid ARIA; only the ds-core output is correct.
knownIssues.fix: Update the docs previews to the anatomy above (grid-wrap > weekdays + grid > week > day).

knownIssues.issue: gds-time-stepper lives in _calendar.scss but uses its own prefix, so it reads like a separate component.
knownIssues.fix: v3: rename to gds-calendar__stepper, or split it into its own component if other screens need a time field.

knownIssues.issue: Range modifiers (--range-start, --in-range, --range-end) are styled, but ds-core has no range mode yet. Products must write range logic themselves.
knownIssues.fix: Add range mode to ds-core (listed as an upcoming phase) or mark the range modifiers beta.

knownIssues.issue: The presets column reuses .gds-menu, which brings its own border, shadow and min-width, so it may show a framed surface inside the calendar surface.
knownIssues.fix: Add a flat menu variant (no border / shadow) or reset them under .gds-calendar__presets. Check visually first.

knownIssues.issue: The state preview helpers .is-hover-preview / .is-focus-preview are also defined for __day (docs only, documented as internal in pagination). They break the BEM naming rule.
knownIssues.fix: v3: one shared preview mechanism (e.g. a data attribute) for all components.

contracts.name: Card
contracts.summary: A container that groups related content and actions, with optional media, header, body and footer.
useWhen: Grouping one object's summary and actions on a dashboard (e.g. an article, a report, a video).
A grid of items people open, with --interactive (e.g. a media library).
Picking one option from a few rich choices, with --selected (e.g. a plan or layout picker).

dontUseWhen.case: Many items with the same fields that people compare or sort
A message that needs attention (success, error, warning)
Content that blocks the page until the user acts
Only adding space or a border around a section of a form
dontUseWhen.use: a plain layout container, no card

anatomy.description: Wrapper. <article> for a self-contained item, <div> for a panel, <a href> when the whole card opens something (with --interactive).

attributes.href: Only on <a>, when the whole card is a link

anatomy.description: Full-bleed image or video at the top, no padding. Put it first.

attributes.alt: On : describe the image, or alt="" if the title already says it all

anatomy.description: Title and subtitle. Draws a separator below when something follows.
Card heading. Pick the level that fits the page outline, not the look.
Secondary line under the title (12px, text-secondary).
Main content. Grows to fill the card height.
Action row, right-aligned. Draws a separator above when something precedes it.

modifiers.description: No border, stronger shadow. Use for cards that float above a grey page.
No border, no shadow, background only. Use for nested or quiet panels.
Pointer cursor, lift and shadow on hover, focus ring on :focus-visible. Use on an <a href> (or a focusable element that opens something).
0 padding in header, body and footer.
12px padding.
24px padding. Without a padding class the card uses 16px.
Inset ring in the focus colour to show the chosen card in a picker. Pair it with a real selected state (aria-checked, aria-pressed or a checked radio).
Dimmed, blocks pointer events and cancels the interactive hover. Does not block the keyboard: also remove href or set aria-disabled and tabindex="-1".

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover on gds-card--interactive (lift + shadow). Turned off by prefers-reduced-motion.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible on gds-card--interactive draws a 2px focus ring.

states.name: selected
states.how: gds-card--selected + aria-checked/aria-pressed or a checked radio inside.

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-card--disabled + no href (or aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="-1").

a11y: An interactive card is one link or button. Do not put other buttons or links inside it.
The card title is a real heading, so people can jump between cards with a screen reader.
--selected and --disabled are only visual: expose the same state with an attribute.
Give images alt text, or alt="" when they only repeat the title.

rules.rule: .gds-card__title is an <h2>–<h4>, never a <div> or <span>.
rules.why: Screen reader users move through a card grid by headings.

rules.rule: A .gds-card--interactive card contains no <button>, <a> or form control.
rules.why: A clickable inside a clickable is a nested interactive element: keyboard and screen readers cannot reach it reliably, and clicks fire twice.

rules.rule: .gds-card--interactive is on an <a href>, a <button>, or an element with tabindex="0" and a role.
rules.why: Hover alone is not an interaction; keyboard users need to reach and open the card.

rules.rule: .gds-card--selected comes with aria-checked="true", aria-pressed="true", or a checked radio inside the card.
rules.why: The ring only shows the choice to sighted users.
rules.removeInV3: Style the selected look from [aria-checked="true"] / :has(:checked), so the class is not needed.

rules.rule: Footer actions use gds-btn, at most one primary, with the primary on the right.
rules.why: Same action order as modals and forms across the product.

rules.rule: Do not build a list of many same-shaped records out of cards; use a table.
rules.why: Tables can be scanned, sorted and selected in bulk; card grids cannot.

internal.why: Docs and screenshot tests only: freezes the hover look of --interactive.
Docs and screenshot tests only: freezes the focus ring of --interactive.

knownIssues.issue: Subtitle colour is now text-secondary (6.96:1, was 2.96:1 and failed AA). Older screenshots, Figma and brand.md may still show the lighter grey.
knownIssues.fix: Update Figma and brand.md to text-secondary; keep the contrast note in the token file.

knownIssues.issue: A card with header and footer but no body draws two separators (header border-bottom + footer border-top), a 2px line.
knownIssues.fix: Draw only one: e.g. .gds-card__header + .gds-card__footer { border-top: 0; }.

knownIssues.issue: An <a class="gds-card gds-card--interactive"> keeps link underline and colour; the docs fix it with inline style="display:block;text-decoration:none".
knownIssues.fix: Add text-decoration: none; color: inherit; to .gds-card--interactive and drop the inline styles from the docs.

knownIssues.issue: --disabled only blocks the mouse (pointer-events: none). A disabled link card can still be focused and opened with Enter.
knownIssues.fix: Document removing href / tabindex="-1"; v3: also style [aria-disabled="true"].

knownIssues.issue: --selected uses the same colour and width as the focus ring, so a selected card looks focused and focus on it is hard to see.
knownIssues.fix: Give selected its own token (e.g. border-brand + check icon) different from border-focus.

contracts.name: Checkbox
contracts.summary: Lets people turn one option on or off, or pick several options from a list.
useWhen: Selecting rows in a table.
Choosing any number of options from a short list.
Agreeing to something before submitting a form.

dontUseWhen.case: A setting that takes effect immediately
Exactly one choice from a list

anatomy.description: Wrapper. A <label>, so clicking the text toggles the box.
Native checkbox, visually hidden but focusable. Its :checked state drives the visual.

attributes.aria-label: Required when there is no visible label (e.g. in table cells)

anatomy.description: The visible box. Must come after the input (CSS uses the ~ sibling selector). Contains the icon: , or "minus" for mixed. Inside a multi-select .gds-dropdown__item it is used on its own, without .gds-checkbox or an (an input is not allowed inside the item button): add aria-hidden="true"; the item carries the state with aria-selected.
Visible label text.
Helper text under the label.

modifiers.description: 16px box. Use in tables.
20px box. Use in forms.
24px box.
Forces the checked look. Prefer the native checked attribute, which works without this class.
Indeterminate (some, not all, selected). Use the minus icon and set input.indeterminate = true in JS.
Disabled look. Also set the disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: checked
states.how: checked attribute on .gds-checkbox__input (CSS reads :checked).

states.name: mixed
states.how: gds-checkbox--mixed + minus icon + input.indeterminate = true.

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-checkbox--disabled + disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible on the input shows a ring on the control.

a11y: Keep the native input: it is what keyboards and screen readers use.
Without visible text, give the input an aria-label ("Select all", "Select <row name>").
For disabled, set the disabled attribute, not only the class.

rules.rule: Every .gds-checkbox contains an <input type="checkbox" class="gds-checkbox__input"> before .gds-checkbox__control.
rules.why: The visual state comes from the input through the ~ selector; without it the box never changes.

rules.rule: A checkbox without .gds-checkbox__label has an aria-label on the input.
rules.why: Otherwise it is announced as an unnamed checkbox.

rules.rule: The control contains the Lucide check icon (or minus for mixed). Do not draw your own SVG.
rules.why: Both AI tests drew their own tick because the guide showed <svg>...</svg>.

rules.rule: Checkboxes in table cells use gds-checkbox--sm.
rules.why: Matches the 16px icon grid of table rows.

knownIssues.issue: Checked can be shown two ways (native checked or gds-checkbox--checked), which can disagree.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drive the look only from the native state; keep --checked for docs previews.

contracts.name: Chip
contracts.summary: A compact token for a tag, a selected value or a toggleable filter, optionally removable, alone, in a group or inside a tag field.
useWhen: Showing tags, categories or people attached to an entry, with an optional remove button.
Quick filters above a list that people switch on and off (selectable chips).
Entering several values in one field: tags, recipients, keywords (chip input).

dontUseWhen.case: A read-only status such as Published or Draft
A count on its own
Opening a filter panel with a count of active filters
A main action

anatomy.description: Wrapping row of chips with even spacing. Can end with a +N counter.
Field that looks like an input and holds chips followed by a text field. Clicking it should focus the field (JS).
The chip. A <span> for static or removable chips; a <button> only with gds-chip--selectable. Medium size by default. Can hold a .gds-avatar (sized automatically) before the label.
Leading Lucide icon (e.g. tag, check). Decorative.
The text. Truncates with an ellipsis.
Remove button after the label: . Only on chips, never inside a
"+N more" at the end of a group. A button that reveals the hidden chips.
Borderless text field after the chips.

attributes.aria-label: Required unless a <label for> points at it, e.g. "Add tag"

modifiers.description: Small. Use inside .gds-chip-input and dense table cells.
Large. Medium is the base size (there is no --md class).
Gray instead of the default blue.
Green.
Orange.
Red.
Fully rounded (pill shape) instead of small corners.
Border and transparent background. Works with the colour variants.
Toggleable filter chip: gray with a border, pointer cursor and focus ring. Put it on a <button>.
Selected (brand fill, white text). Only works together with gds-chip--selectable. Set aria-pressed="true" too.
Faded and ignores the mouse. Also set disabled on the button(s) inside, or on the chip if it is a button.
Makes the +N counter fully rounded. Add it when the chips use gds-chip--rounded.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover darkens the background (on every chip, see knownIssues).

states.name: focus
states.how: Selectable chips show a focus ring on :focus-visible. The close button uses the browser default.

states.name: selected
states.how: gds-chip--selectable + gds-chip--active + aria-pressed="true".

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-chip--disabled + disabled attribute on the chip button or the close button.

states.name: field focus
states.how: Native :focus-within on .gds-chip-input changes its border colour.

a11y: The close button is a real <button type="button"> with aria-label "Remove <label>"; "Remove" alone is ambiguous in a list of chips.
Selectable chips are <button> with aria-pressed reflecting the selected state.
Never put a close button inside a <button> chip or other button: nested interactive elements break keyboard and screen readers.
The chip input field needs an accessible name, and the container should move focus to the field when clicked.
After removing a chip, move focus to the next chip's close button or to the field, so keyboard users are not lost.

rules.rule: Every .gds-chip__close is a <button type="button"> with an aria-label that names the chip.
rules.why: An icon-only x is announced as "button"; with several chips people cannot tell which one it removes.

rules.rule: A gds-chip--selectable is a <button> with aria-pressed, "true" exactly when gds-chip--active is present.
rules.why: The selected state must not be visual only.
rules.removeInV3: Style the selected look from [aria-pressed="true"] so the class and attribute cannot disagree.

rules.rule: A chip without gds-chip--selectable is a <span>, not a <button> or <a>. Removing happens on .gds-chip__close.
rules.why: Only selectable chips have focus styles; a clickable static chip has no visible focus.

rules.rule: A .gds-chip__close is never inside a <button> (a selectable chip, a dropdown trigger or any other).
rules.why: Buttons inside buttons are invalid HTML and cannot be reached reliably by keyboard.

rules.rule: Every .gds-chip-input__field has an aria-label or a <label for>.
rules.why: A placeholder is not a label and disappears once people type.

rules.rule: With gds-chip--disabled, buttons inside the chip (or the chip itself, if it is a button) have the disabled attribute.
rules.why: The class only blocks the mouse; keyboard users could still remove or toggle it.

rules.rule: Chips inside .gds-chip-input use gds-chip--sm.
rules.why: Medium chips make the field taller than a regular input.

rules.rule: Use the default blue for user tags and selected values; use success, warning and error only when the value itself has that meaning.
rules.why: Colour suggests a status; random colours make tags look like warnings.

rules.rule: When the chips in a .gds-chip-group use gds-chip--rounded, the group has gds-chip-group--rounded.
rules.why: Otherwise the +N counter has square corners next to round chips.
rules.removeInV3: Round the counter automatically when the group contains rounded chips (:has).

knownIssues.issue: The SCSS header lists gds-chip--md and gds-chip--avatar, which do not exist. Medium is the base size and avatar chips are a plain .gds-avatar inside .gds-chip.
knownIssues.fix: Update the header comment.

knownIssues.issue: Every chip gets a hover background, including static <span> chips, so read-only tags look clickable.
knownIssues.fix: Apply hover only to selectable chips and to the close button.

knownIssues.issue: gds-chip--active does nothing without gds-chip--selectable.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drive the selected look from aria-pressed="true" on selectable chips and drop --active.

knownIssues.issue: gds-chip--disabled uses pointer-events: none only; the close button stays focusable and works by keyboard.
knownIssues.fix: Require the disabled attribute and style the chip from :disabled / :has(:disabled).

knownIssues.issue: The rule .gds-chip--rounded .gds-chip-group__counter targets a counter inside a chip, which never happens. Docs also omit gds-chip-group--rounded, so the docs counter is square next to rounded chips.
knownIssues.fix: Remove the dead selector and fix the docs example.

knownIssues.issue: The close button is 12–16px with a 6–10px icon, below the 24px minimum target size (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8).
knownIssues.fix: Keep the visual size but add an invisible 24px hit area (padding or ::before).

knownIssues.issue: .gds-chip-input shows focus only as a border colour change and the field removes its outline; other inputs show a focus ring.
knownIssues.fix: Add the input focus ring on :focus-within.

knownIssues.issue: In the docs dropdown example, chips inside the <button> trigger use <span role="button"> close controls, which nests interactive elements.
knownIssues.fix: Move the tags out of the trigger, or make the chips non-removable there.

knownIssues.issue: The selectable focus ring and the chip input borrow input tokens (--input-focus-ring, --input-border) with fallbacks instead of chip tokens.
knownIssues.fix: Add chip focus tokens, or a shared focus token used by all components.

contracts.name: Filter badge
contracts.summary: A compact pill with a filter icon and the number of applied filters; it opens the filter panel.
useWhen: The entry point to filters in a list toolbar (Entries, Assets, Videos), showing how many filters are applied.
Tight spaces where a full "Filters" button does not fit.

dontUseWhen.case: Showing each applied filter value so people can remove it (Status: Published ×)
Showing a status or category
A single filter with a few values

anatomy.description: The pill: light blue background, 24px high, pointer cursor. A <button> that opens the filter panel.

attributes.aria-label: Includes the count, e.g. "Filters, 3 applied" or "Filters"
attributes.aria-haspopup: "dialog" when it opens a filter panel

anatomy.description: Round icon container with the Lucide filter icon (16px, blue).
White circle with the number of applied filters (20px, fixed width). Hidden from screen readers because the button's aria-label says the count.

modifiers.description: At least one filter is applied: adds a blue border.

states.name: no filters
states.how: No --active and no __count; aria-label="Filters".

states.name: filters applied
states.how: gds-filter-badge--active + __count with the number; aria-label="Filters, N applied".

states.name: panel open
states.how: aria-expanded="true" on the button (no visual class).

a11y: Use a <button>, so it is focusable and works with Enter / Space.
The button's aria-label says the count ("Filters, 3 applied"); hide __count with aria-hidden so it is not read twice.
The active state is not colour-only: the count also shows that filters are applied.
There is no visible focus style in the CSS yet (known issue); the browser default outline must not be removed.

rules.rule: .gds-filter-badge is a <button type="button">, never a <span> or <div>.
rules.why: It is clickable (pointer cursor) but a span cannot be reached by keyboard. The docs examples use <span>.

rules.rule: The button has an aria-label that includes the filter count when there is one.
rules.why: Icon plus a bare number is announced as "button, 3".

rules.rule: Show __count and --active together, only when at least one filter is applied; never show a count of 0.
rules.why: One clear meaning: border and number both mean "filters are on".
rules.removeInV3: Drive the border from the count (e.g. :has(.gds-filter-badge__count)) so --active is not needed.

rules.rule: Show at most "9+" in __count.
rules.why: The count circle has a fixed 20px width; longer numbers overflow.
rules.removeInV3: Use min-width and inline padding on __count so any number fits.

rules.rule: Show the applied filter values next to it as removable chips, not as badges.

contracts.summary: A list of actions on demand: overflow ("more") menus, context menus, row actions.
useWhen: Actions on one item that do not fit as buttons (Edit, Duplicate, Move to, Archive, Delete on an article row).
A "more" (ellipsis) button in a toolbar or card.
Right-click / context actions.

dontUseWhen.case: Choosing a value (status, author, category)
One or two main actions
Navigation between pages or sections
A form or other interactive content

Has no open state and no positioning: the product shows / hides it (hidden attribute) and places it next to its trigger. Long menus scroll inside the panel past 360px (or 60% of the screen height): --menu-max-height.

attributes.id: Referenced by aria-controls on the trigger

anatomy.description: Small uppercase heading above a set of items. A sibling of the items, not a wrapper.
One action. Full-width <button>.

attributes.tabindex: -1 (roving: the focused item gets focus via JS)

anatomy.description: Leading icon (16px; 20px in --rich). Decorative.
Rich items only: stacks __label and __desc.

Second line in rich items.
Keyboard shortcut hint on the right (e.g. Ctrl+D).
Trailing icon on the right, e.g. chevron-right for a submenu.
1px line between groups of items.

modifiers.description: Destructive action (Delete): red text and icon.
Not available: faded (opacity), no pointer events. Also set aria-disabled="true".
Two-line item: larger icon + __content with __label and __desc.

states.name: open / closed
states.how: No class. The product toggles the hidden attribute (or wraps the menu in its own positioned layer) and sets aria-expanded on the trigger.

states.name: hover / focus
states.how: Native :hover and :focus-visible on the item.

states.name: disabled item
states.how: gds-menu__item--disabled + aria-disabled="true".

a11y: Container role="menu" with a name; items role="menuitem"; dividers role="separator".
Trigger: <button> with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Keyboard (product JS): Enter / Space / Arrow Down opens and focuses the first item; arrows move; Home / End jump; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Items use roving tabindex (tabindex="-1", focus moved by JS). Disabled items stay focusable with aria-disabled="true" so people can find them.
Icons are decorative: the label carries the meaning.

rules.rule: .gds-menu has role="menu" and an aria-label or aria-labelledby; every .gds-menu__item has role="menuitem".
rules.why: Without roles a screen reader reads a pile of buttons with no menu context or arrow-key hint.

rules.rule: .gds-menu__item is a <button type="button">, never a <div> or <li>.
rules.why: The item styles reset a button; other elements are not focusable or clickable by keyboard.

rules.rule: --disabled items have aria-disabled="true".
rules.why: The class only fades the item; the attribute tells assistive tech it is unavailable.

rules.rule: An item with a chevron-right in __trailing has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded.
rules.why: Announces that the item opens a submenu.

rules.rule: Use menu for actions, dropdown for choosing values.
rules.why: Different semantics (menu vs listbox) and different keyboard models.

rules.rule: Put --danger items last, after a __divider.
rules.why: Separating destructive actions avoids accidental clicks; red text alone is not enough. The action itself should still ask for confirmation (modal) before deleting.

rules.rule: Within a menu, give every item an icon or none.
rules.why: Mixed items make the labels start at different positions and look broken.

knownIssues.issue: No open state and no positioning, unlike gds-dropdown--open and gds-popover--open. Each product invents its own show / hide and placement.
knownIssues.fix: v3: show menus inside .gds-popover (role "menu" on the controller) and drop the menu's own surface.

knownIssues.issue: The menu draws its own background, border and shadow, so inside a .gds-popover or the calendar presets column it gets a second frame.
knownIssues.fix: Add a flat variant, or move the surface to .gds-popover.

knownIssues.issue: The menu uses the dropdown tokens (--dd-*) and has no component tokens of its own.
knownIssues.fix: Add _component-menu.scss tokens that alias the dropdown ones.

knownIssues.issue: --disabled uses opacity 0.4. The calendar dropped opacity for disabled days because it cut contrast to about 1.4:1.
knownIssues.fix: Use a muted text colour token for disabled items, like the calendar.

knownIssues.issue: --disabled sets pointer-events: none and the docs use the disabled attribute, which removes the item from keyboard focus. The ARIA menu pattern keeps disabled items focusable.
knownIssues.fix: Document aria-disabled without the disabled attribute; keep pointer-events: none only for the mouse.

knownIssues.issue: The focus ring is a box-shadow, which disappears in Windows forced-colours mode.
knownIssues.fix: Use outline (as the calendar does) or add a forced-colors fallback.

knownIssues.issue: __group is a sibling label, not a wrapper, so it cannot form an ARIA group; text directly inside role="menu" is not an allowed child.
knownIssues.fix: v3: add a __section wrapper with role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing to __group.

knownIssues.issue: text-align: left and margin-left are physical properties, so items do not mirror in right-to-left layouts.
knownIssues.fix: Use text-align: start and margin-inline-start.

contracts.name: Modal
contracts.summary: A centred dialog over a dimmed page that blocks everything else until the user confirms, decides or cancels.
useWhen: A decision that must be made before going on: "Publish now?", "Discard changes?".
Irreversible or destructive actions (delete entry, unpublish, remove user): use --destructive.
Short, focused tasks with a few fields (rename a tag, merge tags) that make sense without seeing the page.

dontUseWhen.case: Editing entry details while the list or page stays in view
Long forms or many sections
Telling the user something happened
A persistent problem on the page
A confirmation started from inside a side panel
dontUseWhen.use: a confirmation inside the panel (modal z-index is below the panel, known issue)

anatomy.description: Fixed full-screen backdrop that centres the modal. Hidden (opacity 0, visibility hidden) until --open. Product JS may close on backdrop click, except for destructive modals.
The dialog box: white, 640px (md) or 456px (sm), max height viewport minus 64px each side. Full-screen below 640px.
Close button, top-right, first child of the modal. Combine with gds-btn-icon gds-btn-icon--ghost gds-btn-icon--sm gds-btn-icon--circle and a Lucide x icon.
Scroll container with side padding. Header and footer stick to its top and bottom.
Sticky header with title and description.
Dialog title (16px medium). Give it an id for aria-labelledby.
Supporting text (14px). For destructive modals, say what will be lost. Give it an id for aria-describedby.
Content: text, form fields (gds-input, gds-dropdown, gds-checkbox…). Column with 20px gap.
Sticky footer with actions, right-aligned: secondary/ghost first, primary last.

modifiers.description: Shows the overlay and animates the modal in (fade + scale).
456px. Confirmations and one or two fields.
640px. Short forms.
Turns the .gds-btn--primary in the footer red (critical colours). For irreversible actions.
Divider under the header. Product JS adds it when the body is scrolled away from the top.
Divider above the footer. Product JS adds it while there is more content below.
First action left, the rest right (e.g. "Back" left, "Cancel / Next" right).

states.name: closed
states.how: gds-modal-overlay without --open (stays in the DOM, invisible and hidden from assistive tech by visibility: hidden), or not rendered.

states.name: open
states.how: Add gds-modal-overlay--open; then move focus into the modal.

states.name: scrolled
states.how: Toggle __header--scrolled when __inner scrollTop > 0 and __footer--scrolled while it is not scrolled to the end.

a11y: role="dialog" (or "alertdialog" for destructive), aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby on .gds-modal, the element that contains the content.
Destructive modals: role="alertdialog" with aria-describedby on the consequence text.
The close button has aria-label="Close".

Product JS: on open move focus into the modal (first field, or Cancel in a destructive modal), keep Tab inside it, close on Escape, make the page behind inert, and return focus to the trigger on close.
Lock page scroll while open (product JS).

rules.rule: .gds-modal has role="dialog" or "alertdialog", aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing to the id of .gds-modal__title.
rules.why: Screen readers then announce a dialog with its title and treat the page behind as unavailable.

rules.rule: .gds-modal__close is a <button type="button"> with aria-label.
rules.why: It shows only an x icon.

rules.rule: A .gds-modal--destructive uses role="alertdialog" and aria-describedby pointing to .gds-modal__desc, which says what will be lost.
rules.why: The consequence is read out together with the title.

rules.rule: In a destructive modal the confirm button names the action ("Delete entry", "Unpublish"), never "OK" or "Yes". Initial focus goes to Cancel; the backdrop does not close it.
rules.why: People confirm by habit; a specific label and a safe default prevent accidents.

rules.rule: In a .gds-modal--destructive, the confirm button is .gds-btn--primary (the modifier makes it red). Do not add a second primary.
rules.why: The modifier only recolours .gds-btn--primary inside the footer.
rules.removeInV3: Remove --destructive and use .gds-btn--critical in the footer directly.

rules.rule: The footer has at most one .gds-btn--primary, placed last. Cancel uses .gds-btn--ghost.
rules.why: One clear main action, same order in every dialog.

rules.rule: Product JS: on open move focus into the modal (first field, or Cancel in a destructive modal), keep Tab inside it, close on Escape, make the page behind inert, and return focus to the trigger on close.
rules.why: Without it keyboard and screen reader users can reach the page behind or get lost after closing.

rules.rule: Use --sm for confirmations, --md (default) for short forms. Anything longer goes in a side panel or a page.
rules.why: A modal hides the context; long tasks in it are hard to check and easy to lose.

rules.rule: Toggle __header--scrolled and __footer--scrolled from the scroll position of __inner.
rules.why: Shows that content continues under the sticky header or footer.
rules.removeInV3: Use CSS scroll-driven animations so no JS is needed.

rules.rule: Do not open a modal from inside an open side panel.
rules.why: The modal overlay (z-index 1000) renders behind the side panel (1020).
rules.removeInV3: Put the modal above the side panel in the z-index scale.

knownIssues.issue: z-index: modal overlay is 1000, side panel is 1020. A modal opened from a side panel (delete, discard changes) appears behind it.
knownIssues.fix: Raise --modal-z-index above --sidepanel-z-index (e.g. a $z-modal token at 1025).

knownIssues.issue: --destructive re-implements critical button colours on .gds-btn--primary instead of using .gds-btn--critical.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drop --destructive; footer uses .gds-btn--critical.

knownIssues.issue: Docs put role="dialog" and aria-modal on the overlay, and the close buttons have no aria-label.
knownIssues.fix: Move the role to .gds-modal and add aria-label="Close" in the docs.

knownIssues.issue: __header--scrolled / __footer--scrolled need JS to work.
knownIssues.fix: CSS scroll-driven animation or scroll shadows.

knownIssues.issue: Mobile rule uses width: 100% !important and max-height: 100vh (mobile browser bars can cover the footer).
knownIssues.fix: Drop !important; use 100dvh.

knownIssues.issue: --modal-scroll-shadow token is defined but not used.
knownIssues.fix: Remove it or use it for the scroll dividers.

contracts.name: Percentage badge
contracts.summary: A pill that shows how much a metric changed, with an arrow for the direction and a colour for good or bad.
useWhen: Next to a metric on a dashboard or stat card to show change against a previous period (e.g. Page views 1.2M, +12.5%).
In a table column that compares periods (e.g. traffic change per article).

dontUseWhen.case: A status or category (Published, Draft, Sports)
A plain count with no comparison
Something people can click or remove

anatomy.description: Wrapper pill. Neutral grey unless a tone modifier is set.
Direction arrow: Lucide arrow-up (increase) or arrow-down (decrease). Decorative.
The change, e.g. "12.5%". Add the direction as hidden text for screen readers (gds-sr-only).

modifiers.description: Green. The change is good.
Orange. The change needs watching.
Red. The change is bad.
Grey. No change, or the change has no good/bad meaning. Same as the bare class.

a11y: The arrow and colour are visual only. Put the direction in text: increase of before the value, or write the sign (+12.5% / −3.1%).
Hide the arrow icon with aria-hidden="true".
Say what the change compares to near the badge (e.g. "vs last week").

rules.rule: The direction is in text (sr-only text or a +/− sign), not only in the arrow.
rules.why: Screen readers would read "12.5%" with no idea whether it went up or down.

rules.rule: Pick the tone by whether the change is good or bad, not by the arrow: bounce rate up is critical, page views up is positive.
rules.why: Red and green carry meaning; tying them to the arrow gives wrong signals for metrics where lower is better.

rules.rule: arrow-up only with a positive change and arrow-down only with a negative one; a 0% change uses no arrow (or minus) and --neutral.
rules.why: An arrow that disagrees with the number is misleading.

rules.rule: A pct-badge has at most one tone modifier.
rules.why: Two tones produce an undefined colour.

rules.rule: Use pct-badge only for numeric change; statuses and categories use gds-badge.
rules.why: One meaning per component keeps dashboards readable.

knownIssues.issue: The SCSS header lists --up and --down direction classes that do not exist; direction is set only by the icon.
knownIssues.fix: Remove them from the comment, or add them and let CSS draw the arrow so the icon cannot disagree.

knownIssues.issue: There is no size option (fixed 26px high, 14px text), so the badge is too big for dense table rows.
knownIssues.fix: Add --sm matching gds-badge--sm if tables need it.

knownIssues.issue: The docs show only the arrow for direction, with no text alternative.
knownIssues.fix: Add gds-sr-only direction text to the docs examples.

attributes.aria-hidden: "true" when nearby text already says the count; otherwise add visually hidden context, e.g. "3 unread notifications"

modifiers.description: 16px. Next to icons (notification bell) and small labels.
20px. Tabs and menu items. Same as the base size.
24px. Step numbers.
Gray. Passive counts. Same as the base colour.
Red. Counts that need action: errors, failed items, urgent notifications.
Green. Completed steps or successful items.
Orange. Counts that need attention soon (items expiring, pending review).
Purple. Category counts with no status meaning.
No background, gray number. Upcoming steps.
Solid fill with white text instead of the light tint. Combine with a tone (alone it is dark gray). Do not combine with --blank: dark overrides it.

a11y: A number alone means nothing to a screen reader: either the visible label next to it says what is counted, or add visually hidden text such as "3 unread notifications".
When the count changes live (new notifications), announce the change in a polite live region elsewhere, not on every pill.
Do not show meaning by colour alone: the label or the step text must say it too.
Light tones meet text contrast except warning (just under 4.5:1); dark tones do not (see knownIssues).

rules.rule: A .gds-pill contains a number of one or two characters (e.g. 3, 12, 9+). Never words.
rules.why: The width is fixed, so longer text is cut off; words belong in a badge.
rules.removeInV3: Give the pill a min-width and padding so longer counts (99+) grow instead of clipping.

rules.rule: Every pill sits next to text that says what is counted, or contains visually hidden text that does.
rules.why: "3" alone does not tell anyone what there are three of.

rules.rule: A .gds-pill is never a <button> or <a>; make the parent tab, menu item or button clickable instead.
rules.why: Pills have no hover or focus styles, and a 16–24px target is too small.

rules.rule: A pill has at most one tone class; gds-pill--dark is not combined with gds-pill--blank.
rules.why: Two tones give an undefined colour, and dark silently overrides blank.

rules.rule: Use gds-pill--dark for counts that ask for action (unread, errors); use the light style for passive totals.
rules.why: The solid fill pulls the eye; keep it for things people should act on.

knownIssues.issue: Width is fixed per size and overflow is hidden, so three or more characters (100, 99+) are clipped.
knownIssues.fix: Use min-width plus horizontal padding instead of a fixed width.

knownIssues.issue: White text on the dark tones is below 4.5:1: warning about 2.5:1, purple and critical about 3.5:1, positive about 4:1.
knownIssues.fix: Use the 700 shades for dark backgrounds, or dark text on warning.

knownIssues.issue: Light warning (orange-700 on orange-50) is about 4.35:1, just under 4.5:1 for small text.
knownIssues.fix: Use orange-900 text, as the warning chip does.

knownIssues.issue: gds-pill--dark and gds-pill--blank have the same specificity and dark comes later, so blank + dark renders as dark gray.
knownIssues.fix: Scope --dark rules to exclude --blank, or document the pair as invalid (rule pill-one-tone).

knownIssues.issue: The name collides with gds-btn--pill and "pill shape" chips, which mean rounded corners, while this component is a number count. brand.md even shows text like "On Track" in a pill, which gets clipped.
knownIssues.fix: v3: rename to gds-count. Now: fix the brand.md example.

contracts.name: Popover
contracts.summary: A generic floating surface anchored to a trigger, for interactive content such as a small form, a calendar or a menu.
useWhen: Interactive content that belongs to one control and should not leave the page context (embed code with a Copy button, quick edit of a title, column settings).
Hosting another component that has to float: the date picker calendar.
Content that must escape a clipping container (table cell, modal, scrolling panel).

dontUseWhen.case: A short, non-interactive hint on hover or focus
A list of actions (Edit, Duplicate, Delete)
Choosing a value from a list
A task that needs full attention or a confirmation (Delete article?)

anatomy.description: The surface: light background, border, radius, shadow, max-height with scroll. position: fixed by default; the createPopover() controller writes top / left inline. Hidden (opacity + visibility) until --open.

attributes.id: Referenced by aria-controls on the trigger
attributes.role: dialog (default) | menu | listbox | grid, set by the controller from its role option
attributes.aria-label: Name of the surface, e.g. "Embed code" (or aria-labelledby a heading inside)

anatomy.description: Padding wrapper (--popover-padding). Leave it out when the content brings its own spacing (e.g. .gds-calendar).
Optional decorative diamond pointing at the trigger. The controller positions it (arrow option).

modifiers.description: Visible. Toggled by the controller together with aria-expanded on the trigger.

states.name: open
states.how: gds-popover--open on the surface + aria-expanded="true" on the trigger (both set by createPopover()).

states.name: closed
states.how: No --open. The element stays in the DOM (it fades out and Floating UI can measure it).

a11y: Trigger: a <button> with aria-haspopup (matching the role), aria-controls = popover id and aria-expanded. createPopover() sets all three.
Surface: a role (dialog by default) and an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby).
Escape and outside click close it; focus moves into the surface on open and back to the trigger on close (controller).
Modal mode traps focus and makes the background inert; use it only when the popover must be finished before going on.
Reduced motion: the open / close transition snaps. Forced colours: the border stays visible.

rules.rule: The trigger has aria-haspopup, aria-controls pointing to the popover id, and aria-expanded matching gds-popover--open.
rules.why: Screen readers announce that the button opens something and whether it is open.

rules.rule: A .gds-popover with role="dialog" has aria-label or aria-labelledby.
rules.why: An unnamed dialog is announced as just "dialog".

rules.rule: .gds-popover__arrow has aria-hidden="true".
rules.why: It is decoration only.

rules.rule: Position, open and dismiss the popover with createPopover() from @gjirafa/ds-core; do not hand-write top / left.
rules.why: The controller handles flip, shift, scroll, portal out of clipping parents, Escape and focus return; the CSS alone puts the surface at the top-left of the viewport.
rules.removeInV3: Use CSS anchor positioning once browser support allows, so a CSS-only popover can place itself.

rules.rule: Wrap plain content in __content; put components with their own padding (.gds-calendar) directly in .gds-popover.
rules.why: Otherwise the padding is doubled.

rules.rule: Use a popover for interactive content opened by a click; use a tooltip for short text on hover or focus.
rules.why: A popover takes focus and needs a click to open; a tooltip must never hold controls.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-calendar-popover duplicates this surface (same border, radius, shadow) with its own absolute positioning.
knownIssues.fix: Rebuild .gds-calendar-popover on .gds-popover (already planned in the popover docs).

knownIssues.issue: .gds-menu and .gds-dropdown__panel carry their own background, border and shadow. Putting them in a .gds-popover draws two frames.
knownIssues.fix: v3: menu and dropdown panel take their surface from .gds-popover (or get a flat variant).

knownIssues.issue: Without the controller the surface is position: fixed with no coordinates, so it shows at the top-left of the viewport.
knownIssues.fix: Document the controller as required; later add CSS anchor positioning as a fallback.

knownIssues.issue: The arrow is a rotated square in the surface colour with no border, while the surface has a 1px border. The arrow may look cut off from the frame. Needs a visual check.
knownIssues.fix: Give the arrow the same border on its two outer sides.

knownIssues.issue: Open state naming differs across overlays: gds-popover--open, gds-dropdown--open, gds-calendar-popover--open, and is-open on the tooltip and the table action menu.
knownIssues.fix: v3: one convention for every overlay (e.g. --open on the surface).

contracts.name: Radio
contracts.summary: Lets people pick exactly one option from a short, visible list.
useWhen: Exactly one choice from 2 to about 6 options that people should see side by side (e.g. Visibility: Public / Unlisted / Private).
The options need a short explanation each (use __helper).

dontUseWhen.case: Any number of options can be chosen
A single on/off setting
More than about 6 options, or the list is long
Switching between views of the same content

anatomy.description: One option. A <label>, so clicking the text selects it. Put all options of a group in a <fieldset> with a <legend> (or role="radiogroup" with aria-labelledby); GDS has no class for the group.
Native radio, visually hidden but focusable. Its :checked state drives the visual. Must come before the control (CSS uses ~).

attributes.name: Same value for every option in the group

anatomy.description: The visible circle.
Inner dot, shown when checked. Without it the checked radio is a filled circle with no dot.
Visible label text. Stacks its children in a column, so the helper goes inside it.
Helper line under the label text (12px, text-secondary). Put it inside __label.

modifiers.description: 16px circle, 12px label. Use in dense panels and tables.
20px circle, 14px label. Use in forms.
24px circle, 16px label.
Forces the checked look. Prefer the native checked attribute, which works without this class.
Disabled look. Also set the disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: checked
states.how: checked attribute on one .gds-radio__input of the group (CSS reads :checked).

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-radio--disabled + disabled attribute on the input (or on the <fieldset> for the whole group).

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible on the input shows a ring on the control.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover on the wrapper darkens the circle border.

a11y: Keep the native input: browsers then give arrow-key movement inside the group for free.
All options in a group share one name, so only one can be checked.
Wrap the group in <fieldset> + <legend> (or role="radiogroup" + aria-labelledby) so the question is read with each option.
Helper text inside __label becomes part of the option's name; keep it short.

rules.rule: Every .gds-radio contains <input type="radio" class="gds-radio__input"> before .gds-radio__control.
rules.why: The visual state comes from the input through the ~ selector; without it the circle never changes.

rules.rule: Every radio input has a name, and the options of one group share it.
rules.why: Without a shared name each radio acts alone: several can be checked and arrow keys do not move between them.

rules.rule: A group of .gds-radio sits in a <fieldset> with a <legend>, or in an element with role="radiogroup" and an accessible name.
rules.why: Screen readers read the question ("Visibility") with each option.

rules.rule: Exactly one option in a group is checked by default, unless having no answer is meaningful.
rules.why: A radio group cannot be cleared once picked; start from a sensible default.

rules.rule: A group has at least 2 options; for a single yes/no use a checkbox or toggle.
rules.why: A single radio cannot be turned off.

knownIssues.issue: Disabled + checked looks different depending on how checked is set: with the native :checked the circle stays primary blue and still changes colour on hover; with --checked alone it turns grey.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drive the look only from the native state and add .gds-radio__input:disabled styles that win over :checked.

knownIssues.issue: Disabled is class-only; a native disabled input (or disabled fieldset) without the class still looks enabled.
knownIssues.fix: v3: style from .gds-radio__input:disabled ~ .gds-radio__control and the label.

knownIssues.issue: __helper sits inside __label here (the label is a flex column), but the checkbox contract places __helper next to __label. The CSS is the same for both.
knownIssues.fix: Pick one structure (inside __label) and align the checkbox contract and docs.

knownIssues.issue: There is no class for the group (spacing, legend style). Each product builds its own wrapper.
knownIssues.fix: Add .gds-radio-group (and reuse it for checkbox groups) with gap and legend styles.

knownIssues.issue: __helper keeps text-secondary when the option is disabled, while the label turns text-disabled.
knownIssues.fix: Dim the helper in .gds-radio--disabled too.
