contracts.name: Side panel
contracts.summary: A full-height panel that slides in from the right over a dimmed page, for editing or viewing details while the underlying list stays visible.
useWhen: Editing the details of an item picked from a list (entry metadata, SEO fields, tag settings) while the list stays visible behind.
Viewing details of a row without leaving the page (author profile, asset info, version history).
Forms that are too long for a modal but do not need their own page.
Settings or filters that apply to the page behind (--default, 300px).

dontUseWhen.case: A yes/no decision or confirmation
Destructive confirmation started from the panel
dontUseWhen.use: an inline confirmation inside the panel (a modal would open behind it, known issue)

dontUseWhen.case: The main editing task of a page (writing the article body)
A short message

anatomy.description: Fixed full-screen backdrop; aligns the panel to the right. Hidden until --open. Product JS may close on backdrop click when there are no unsaved changes.
The panel: full height, white, rounded left corners, slides in from the right. 500px unless a size modifier is set. Full width below 640px (and below its own width for --lg/--xl).

attributes.aria-labelledby: id of .gds-sidepanel__title (or of __topbar-title when there is no header)

anatomy.description: 40px bar with a bottom border: __topbar-title on the left, close button on the right. The close button is a gds-btn-icon gds-btn-icon--ghost gds-btn-icon--xs with aria-label="Close" (no element class of its own).
Small title (14px medium, one line, ellipsis). Names the object being viewed or edited, e.g. the entry title.
Scroll container (left padding only; children add right padding). Holds header, body and footer.
Sticky header with the task title and description.
Task title (16px medium). Give it an id for aria-labelledby.
Supporting text (14px).
Content: fields, lists, details. Column with 20px gap.
Sticky footer with actions, right-aligned: ghost first, primary last. Must be inside __content (it relies on its left padding).

modifiers.description: Shows the overlay and slides the panel in.
300px. Despite the name it is NOT the default; use for narrow filters or settings.
500px. Same as no modifier. Most edit forms.
850px. Rich details: media, previews, two-column forms.
1170px. Near full-screen work (comparing versions).
Divider under the header. Product JS adds it when __content is scrolled.
Divider above the footer. Product JS adds it while there is more content below.
First action left, the rest right (e.g. "Delete" left, "Cancel / Save" right).

states.name: closed
states.how: gds-sidepanel-overlay without --open (invisible and hidden from assistive tech by visibility: hidden), or not rendered.

states.name: open
states.how: Add gds-sidepanel-overlay--open; then move focus into the panel.

states.name: scrolled
states.how: Toggle __header--scrolled when __content scrollTop > 0 and __footer--scrolled while it is not scrolled to the end.

a11y: role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby on .gds-sidepanel. The overlay blocks the page, so the panel is modal.
The topbar close button is an icon button with aria-label="Close".
Product JS: on open move focus to the first field (or the panel title), keep Tab inside the panel, close on Escape, make the page behind inert, and return focus to the trigger on close.
If there are unsaved changes, ask before closing (product JS); do not lose input on Escape or backdrop click.

rules.rule: .gds-sidepanel has role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing to the panel title.
rules.why: Screen readers announce a dialog with its name and ignore the page behind.

rules.rule: The close button in .gds-sidepanel__topbar is a <button type="button"> with aria-label.
rules.why: It shows only an x icon.
rules.removeInV3: Add a .gds-sidepanel__close element like .gds-modal__close.

rules.rule: .gds-sidepanel__footer is inside .gds-sidepanel__content.
rules.why: The footer has only right padding; outside __content it touches the left edge and does not stick.
rules.removeInV3: Give the footer its own full padding so it can be a direct child of the panel.

rules.rule: Leave the size as default (--normal, 500px) for edit forms; --lg/--xl only for media or side-by-side content; --default (300px) only for filters or settings.
rules.why: Wider panels hide more of the list the user wants to keep in view.
rules.removeInV3: Rename sizes to sm/md/lg/xl with md as the default.

rules.rule: __topbar-title names the object ("Summer festival guide"); __title names the task ("Edit details"). If you show only one, label the dialog with it.
rules.why: Two similar titles stacked read as a repeat; distinct roles make each useful.

rules.rule: The footer has at most one .gds-btn--primary, placed last. Cancel uses .gds-btn--ghost.
rules.why: One clear main action, same order as in modals.

rules.rule: Product JS: on open move focus to the first field (or the panel title), keep Tab inside the panel, close on Escape, make the page behind inert, and return focus to the trigger on close.
rules.why: Without it keyboard and screen reader users can reach the page behind or get lost after closing.

rules.rule: Do not open a modal from inside the panel; confirm inside the panel instead.
rules.why: The modal (z-index 1000) renders behind the panel (1020).
rules.removeInV3: Put the modal above the side panel in the z-index scale.

knownIssues.issue: --default is 300px, but the real default (no modifier) is 500px (= --normal).
knownIssues.fix: v3: sizes sm 300 / md 500 / lg 850 / xl 1170, md default; keep old names as aliases for one release.

knownIssues.issue: Footer placement differs: the SCSS comment and live docs put __footer inside __content; the docs "Show code" puts it after __content, where it has no left padding.
knownIssues.fix: Fix the docs snippet, or give the footer full padding so both work.

knownIssues.issue: No close element class (modal has __close); docs use gds-btn-icon--xs without aria-label, while the modal uses --sm --circle.
knownIssues.fix: Add .gds-sidepanel__close and use the same button style as the modal.

knownIssues.issue: Two titles (__topbar-title and __title) with no guidance; docs examples use different text in each.
knownIssues.fix: Agree on their roles (see rule sidepanel-titles) or drop one.

knownIssues.issue: z-index 1020 is above the modal (1000), so modals opened from a panel are hidden.
knownIssues.fix: Modal above side panel in the z-index scale.

knownIssues.issue: Docs put role="dialog" on the overlay instead of the panel.
knownIssues.fix: Move role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby to .gds-sidepanel in the docs.

knownIssues.issue: Always modal (backdrop blocks the list); there is no docked, non-modal variant for editing while still using the list.
knownIssues.fix: v3: optional non-modal panel without overlay.

knownIssues.issue: height: 100vh can be covered by mobile browser bars; width: 100% !important on mobile.
knownIssues.fix: Use 100dvh; drop !important.

knownIssues.issue: --sidepanel-footer-padding and --sidepanel-scroll-shadow tokens are defined but not used.
knownIssues.fix: Remove them or use them.

contracts.name: Skeleton
contracts.summary: Grey shimmering shapes that stand in for content while it loads, so the layout does not jump.
useWhen: First load of a page or card whose layout is known (article list, profile header, dashboard card).
Loading takes long enough to notice (about 300ms or more).

dontUseWhen.case: A table is loading
An action the user just triggered (save, upload, publish)
dontUseWhen.use: button loading state or a spinner

dontUseWhen.case: The layout of the result is unknown or loading is very short
There is no data (not loading)

anatomy.description: Stacks skeletons in a column (or a row with --row) with the standard gap. Hide it from screen readers.
One placeholder shape. Full width, rectangle by default. Use a shape modifier to say what it stands for.

attributes.aria-hidden: true (unless its group already has it)

modifiers.description: A line of text: pill radius, body-sm height.
Rectangle for an image or hero. Same as the bare class; write it for clarity.
Circle, avatar-md size unless you set width and height.
Full-width bar at data-table row height.
Circle at avatar sm size.
Circle at avatar md size.
Circle at avatar lg size.
Circle at avatar xl size.
Text line height for small text. Sets only the height: add --text for the pill shape.
Body-sm line height (same as --text alone).
Large text line height.
Heading line height.
Large heading line height.
25% width.
50% width.
75% width. Use on the last line of a paragraph.
Lays skeletons out in a row, vertically centred (e.g. avatar next to text lines).

states.name: loading
states.how: Skeletons are shown; the region they sit in has aria-busy="true".

states.name: loaded
states.how: Replace the skeletons with the real content and set aria-busy="false" (or remove it).

states.name: reduced motion
states.how: prefers-reduced-motion stops the shimmer and shows a static, dimmed shape. Automatic.

a11y: Skeletons are decorative: aria-hidden="true" on the group or on each skeleton.
Set aria-busy="true" on the region that is loading, and give it a short text for screen readers (e.g. Loading articles).
When loading ends, remove aria-busy so the new content is read.

rules.rule: Every .gds-skeleton has aria-hidden="true" itself or on an ancestor.
rules.why: Otherwise screen readers find empty, meaningless elements.

rules.rule: Skeletons sit inside an element with aria-busy="true" that also contains loading text for screen readers.
rules.why: Screen reader users must know the page is loading, not empty.

rules.rule: The skeleton copies the shape of the content it replaces: same number of lines, avatar size, image ratio.
rules.why: The page should not jump when content arrives.

rules.rule: Do not use .gds-skeleton inside .gds-table; use gds-table--loading and gds-table__skeleton.
rules.why: The table has its own loading pattern sized to its cells.
rules.removeInV3: Merge gds-table__skeleton into gds-skeleton so there is one loading shape.

rules.rule: A --text-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl line also has --text.
rules.why: The size classes set only the height; without --text the line has square corners.
rules.removeInV3: Give the --text-* sizes the pill radius, so --text is not needed with them.

knownIssues.issue: --text-sm/lg/xl/2xl set only the height. Alone they give a square-cornered bar; the docs use --text-xl without --text.
knownIssues.fix: Move the pill radius into each --text-* class (or document the pair) and fix the docs examples.

knownIssues.issue: --row says it matches .gds-data-table rows, a class that no longer exists; the table also has its own gds-table__skeleton.
knownIssues.fix: Point --row at the gds-table row height, or remove it in favour of gds-table__skeleton.

knownIssues.issue: --rect is identical to the bare class, and --circle overlaps the --avatar-* presets.
knownIssues.fix: v3: keep one way: e.g. --circle + avatar size tokens, and drop --rect or make it the documented default.

knownIssues.issue: No helper for the screen-reader loading text; every product must remember aria-busy and an sr-only label.
knownIssues.fix: Document the pattern in the docs page and show it in every example.

contracts.name: Status dot
contracts.summary: A small coloured dot that shows someone's presence (online, away, busy, offline), always next to text or with a label.
useWhen: Showing whether a person is online, away, busy or offline in a list of users or collaborators.
Live presence of editors on an entry (who is editing now).

dontUseWhen.case: The status of content (Published, Draft, Scheduled)
Online status on a photo avatar
dontUseWhen.use: avatar (.gds-avatar__status) for online; see knownIssues for other states

dontUseWhen.case: A count

anatomy.description: The dot. Empty element; 8px gray (offline) by default. Place it before a text label.

attributes.aria-hidden: "true" when the status is written in text next to it
attributes.role: "img" when there is no text next to it

modifiers.description: 6px. Dense lists and small avatars.
8px. Same as the base size.
10px.
12px. Large avatars and profile headers.
Green. Active now.
Gray. Not active. Same as the base colour.
Red. Do not disturb.
Orange. Idle or away.
Blue. Not a presence state; use only for a custom state you name in text.
Purple. Not a presence state; use only for a custom state you name in text.
Adds a white ring (outside the dot) so it stays visible on photos and coloured backgrounds.

a11y: A dot is colour only. Write the status in text next to it (and hide the dot with aria-hidden="true"), or give it role="img" and aria-label.
aria-label on a plain <span> is ignored by most screen readers; it needs role="img".
Offline and away dots are below 3:1 against white (see knownIssues), so text next to them matters even more.

rules.rule: Every .gds-status-dot either has aria-hidden="true" with the status written next to it, or has role="img" and an aria-label.
rules.why: Colour alone does not reach colour-blind or screen-reader users.

rules.rule: A status dot has exactly one state class, even for offline.
rules.why: Writing the state makes the markup readable and avoids two colours fighting.
rules.removeInV3: Keep the base gray and make the state optional only if offline stays the documented default.

rules.rule: Use status dots for people's presence. For content or process status use a badge with a dot.

rules.rule: Add gds-status-dot--ring when the dot sits on a photo, avatar or coloured surface.
rules.why: Without the ring the dot blends into the image.

rules.rule: A status dot is never a <button> or <a> and never the only content of one.
rules.why: At 6–12px it is far too small to hit and has no focus style.

knownIssues.issue: Offline (neutral-80) is about 3:1 and away (orange-500) about 2.5:1 against white, below the 3:1 needed for meaningful graphics.
knownIssues.fix: Darken the offline and away tokens, or always require text (rule status-dot-labelled).

knownIssues.issue: info and purple are not presence states, so the set mixes presence and decoration.
knownIssues.fix: v3: keep online/away/busy/offline; move other colours to badge dots.

knownIssues.issue: Avatars have their own .gds-avatar__status that is always green; a status-dot cannot be placed in the avatar corner without custom CSS.
knownIssues.fix: Allow .gds-status-dot--ring inside .gds-avatar in the status position and deprecate __status.

knownIssues.fix: Update brand.md.

Key/value details of a single record

Selection count, e.g. "2 selected".
Vertical separator between count and actions.
One bulk action.
Optional wrapper for horizontal scroll. Wraps .gds-table.

rules.rule: The bulk-action bar sits directly above .gds-table (or .gds-table-scroll) and is shown with is-visible only while rows are selected.

a11y: Use the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" on .gds-tabs, role="tab" on each .gds-tab, role="tabpanel" on each panel.
Each tab has aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel has an id and aria-labelledby pointing back at its tab, plus tabindex="0" when it has no focusable content.
Keyboard: Tab enters the list on the active tab; Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tabs; Home/End go to the first/last. The CSS does not do this; the product JS must.
Hide inactive panels with the hidden attribute so they are not read.
The status dot is colour only: add new next to it.

rules.rule: .gds-tabs has role="tablist" and every .gds-tab has role="tab".

rules.rule: Exactly one .gds-tab has gds-tab--active, and it is the only tab with aria-selected="true".
rules.why: The class draws the selection, the attribute announces it; they must agree.
rules.removeInV3: Style the active tab from [aria-selected="true"], so the class is not needed.

rules.rule: Every .gds-tab has aria-controls pointing to an element with role="tabpanel".
rules.why: Links each tab to the content it shows.

rules.rule: A gds-tab--icon-only tab has an aria-label.
rules.why: An icon alone has no accessible name.

rules.rule: Do not use tabs to link to other pages; use navigation with links and aria-current.
rules.why: Tabs switch content in place; pages change the URL and need real links.

rules.rule: A .gds-tabs has at most one of --filled and --card.
rules.why: The two looks override each other.

knownIssues.issue: The docs build tabs as <nav> with plain buttons: no role="tablist"/"tab", no aria-selected, no panels.

knownIssues.issue: The closable tab in the docs is a <div class="gds-tab"> with a button inside. As role="tab" this is a nested control, and the div is not focusable. .gds-tab__close also has no :focus-visible style.
knownIssues.fix: Support Delete to close on the focused tab and make the close button tabindex="-1", or move the close button outside the tab element; add a focus style to __close.

knownIssues.issue: --active and --disabled are classes only; nothing ties them to aria-selected / aria-disabled. --disabled uses pointer-events: none, so keyboard users can still activate it.
knownIssues.fix: v3: style from [aria-selected="true"] and [aria-disabled="true"].

knownIssues.issue: In --vertical the active tab text uses the hover colour (text-primary) while the other variants use action-primary.
knownIssues.fix: Confirm with design; if not intended, use --tab-color-active in vertical too.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-tabs-wrap and its fade modifiers are not shown in the docs and need JS that GDS does not ship.
knownIssues.fix: Add a docs example with the small scroll script, or remove the wrapper.

knownIssues.issue: --vertical combined with --filled or --card is not designed; the styles mix.
knownIssues.fix: Document as unsupported, or add a check.

contracts.name: Toast
contracts.summary: A short, single-line floating message that confirms something just happened and goes away on its own.
useWhen: Confirming an action the user just took: "Article published", "Entry deleted", "Link copied".
Offering one quick follow-up such as Undo or View.
Background events that do not need action now ("Draft auto-saved").

dontUseWhen.case: An error the user must read or fix (failed publish, validation)
A message longer than one short sentence, or with a title
A decision the user must make
The only way to reach an important action
dontUseWhen.use: a button in the page; the toast can repeat it

anatomy.description: Fixed stack at a screen edge. Put it in the page once (empty) so it can act as a live region; toasts are added inside it. Needs one position modifier.
The toast. Flex row: icon block, body. Usually inside gds-toast-container.

attributes.role: "alert" only on --critical toasts; others rely on the container's role="status".

anatomy.description: Solid colour block on the left with a white 24px Lucide icon. Colour comes from the variant.
Row with text, action and timer.
The message. One line; longer text is cut with an ellipsis.
One text button (Undo, View, Retry).
Round countdown badge (26px). Contains a <span> with the seconds left and the __timer-ring SVG. Product JS updates both.
Progress ring: <svg viewBox="0 0 29 29"> with one <circle cx="14.5" cy="14.5" r="12.5">. JS sets stroke-dasharray/offset (circumference ≈ 78.5).

modifiers.description: Purple icon block and ring. Neutral events.
Green. Action completed.
Orange. Completed, but with something to note.
Red. Something failed in the background; keep it short and offer Retry.
Fades and slides out. Add with JS, then remove the element after the transition.
24px from the top and right edges.
24px from the top and left edges.
Top, centred.
24px from the bottom and right edges.
24px from the bottom and left edges.
Bottom, centred.

states.name: counting down
states.how: Product JS updates the timer <span> text, its aria-label and the ring circle stroke-dashoffset each second.

states.name: dismissing
states.how: Add gds-toast--dismissing, wait for the transition (normal duration), then remove the element.

a11y: The container is in the DOM before any toast is added, with role="status" and aria-live="polite", so new toasts are announced.
--critical toasts get role="alert" so they are announced at once.
Auto-dismiss timing is product JS: at least 5 seconds, longer with an action, and the timer pauses on hover and on focus inside the toast.
The action is a real <button>. Moving focus into a toast is never automatic; keyboard users must be able to reach it (e.g. a shortcut or it stays until focus leaves).
The icon is decorative; the text carries the meaning.
Timer: role="timer" with an aria-label; the ring SVG is aria-hidden.

rules.rule: Toasts live inside a .gds-toast-container with role="status" and aria-live="polite" that exists before toasts are added. --critical toasts add role="alert".
rules.why: A live region only announces content added after it exists.

rules.rule: .gds-toast-container has exactly one position modifier. Default choice: --top-right.
rules.why: Without one the fixed container has no offsets and lands in an arbitrary spot.
rules.removeInV3: Make --top-right the default position of .gds-toast-container.

rules.rule: Toast text is one short sentence (about 60 characters or less), with no title and no links inside the text.
rules.why: __text never wraps; longer text is cut with an ellipsis and cannot be read.
rules.removeInV3: Allow two lines with line-clamp and expose the full text.

rules.rule: An auto-dismissing toast stays at least 5 seconds (10 with an action) and pauses on hover and focus.
rules.why: People need time to read and to reach the action (WCAG 2.2.1).

rules.rule: .gds-toast__action is a <button type="button">; at most one per toast.
rules.why: It must be reachable with the keyboard, and one action keeps the toast quick to read.

rules.rule: .gds-toast__timer has role="timer" and an aria-label; .gds-toast__timer-ring has aria-hidden="true".
rules.why: The number alone has no context for screen readers, and the ring is decoration.

rules.rule: .gds-toast__icon has aria-hidden="true"; icons: info → info, success → check, warning → alert-triangle, critical → x-circle.
rules.why: The meaning is in the text; same icon for the same meaning, as in the docs.

rules.rule: A toast has exactly one variant class. Write --info explicitly.
rules.why: Two variants give an undefined colour.

rules.rule: Errors the user has to fix are shown as an inline alert, not a toast.
rules.why: Toasts disappear; an error that vanishes leaves the user without a way to fix it.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-toast-container is defined twice: in _alert.scss (max-width 400px) and _toast.scss (max-width 490px). The toast file wins only because it loads later.
knownIssues.fix: Define the container once, in _toast.scss.

knownIssues.issue: The docs never show __timer / __timer-ring markup. The ring geometry exists only as a JS constant (r = 12.5) and the ring is offset to sit over the border. brand.md puts the timer outside __body, but __body's right padding suggests inside.
knownIssues.fix: Document the SVG markup (viewBox, circle) in the docs, or replace the SVG with a CSS-only ring (conic-gradient + a registered custom property).

knownIssues.issue: There is no close element. A toast without a timer (docs: "Action without timer") cannot be dismissed.
knownIssues.fix: Add .gds-toast__close (24px+ icon button).

knownIssues.issue: White icon on the warning block (orange-500) is 2.5:1, below the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum. Info 3.5:1, critical 3.6:1, success 4.0:1 pass.
knownIssues.fix: Use a darker orange for --toast-warning-bg or a dark icon on warning.

knownIssues.issue: __text is nowrap with ellipsis; longer messages are cut with no way to read them.
knownIssues.fix: Allow up to two lines (line-clamp) and keep the full text available.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-toast:hover changes the background, which suggests the whole toast is clickable. It is not.
knownIssues.fix: Remove the hover background.

knownIssues.issue: Naming: toast uses --critical, alert uses --error. Toast info is purple, badge info is blue.
knownIssues.fix: Align variant names and the info colour across components.

contracts.name: Toggle
contracts.summary: An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect immediately.
useWhen: A setting that applies the moment it is flipped, with no Save button (e.g. Email notifications, Auto-publish).
Turning a feature or a single item on and off in a list (e.g. enable a plugin, show a section on the homepage).

dontUseWhen.case: A choice that is submitted later with a form button
Picking several options from a list
Picking one of two or more named options (e.g. Public / Private)
An action that runs once (e.g. Publish now)

anatomy.description: Wrapper. A <label>, so clicking the text flips the switch.
Native checkbox with the switch role, visually hidden but focusable. Its :checked state drives the visual. Must come before the track (CSS uses ~).

attributes.aria-label: Required when there is no visible label
attributes.aria-describedby: Optional: id of help text outside the toggle

anatomy.description: The pill-shaped track. Grey when off, primary colour when on.
The round knob. Slides right when on.
Visible label text, after the track. Name the setting, not the state ("Email notifications", not "On").

modifiers.description: 32×16 track, 12px label. Use in dense lists and table rows.
40×20 track, 14px label. Use in forms and settings.
48×24 track, 16px label.
Forces the on look. Prefer the native checked attribute, which works without this class.
Disabled look. Also set the disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: on
states.how: checked attribute on .gds-toggle__input (CSS reads :checked). role="switch" makes screen readers say on/off.

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-toggle--disabled + disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible on the input shows a ring around the track.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover on the wrapper darkens the track.

a11y: Use the native checkbox with role="switch": keyboard (Space) and screen readers work, and the checked state is announced as on/off. Do not add aria-checked; the native checked state is enough.
Without visible text, give the input an aria-label that names the setting.
The change applies immediately: if it can fail, tell the user (toast) and flip it back.
For disabled, set the disabled attribute, not only the class.

rules.rule: Every .gds-toggle contains <input type="checkbox" role="switch" class="gds-toggle__input"> before .gds-toggle__track.
rules.why: The visual state comes from the input through the ~ selector, and role="switch" makes it announced as on/off instead of checked.

rules.rule: A toggle without .gds-toggle__label has an aria-label on the input.
rules.why: Otherwise it is announced as an unnamed switch.

rules.rule: Use a toggle only when flipping it applies the change right away; inside a form that is submitted with a button, use a checkbox.
rules.why: A switch looks like a light switch: people expect the effect now. Mixing the two makes people unsure whether they must save.

rules.rule: The label names the setting and does not change with the state (not "On"/"Off").
rules.why: The switch already shows the state; a changing label makes it unclear what the switch controls.

rules.rule: gds-toggle--disabled always comes with the disabled attribute on the input.
rules.why: The class only changes the look; without the attribute the switch still works from the keyboard.
rules.removeInV3: Style disabled from .gds-toggle__input:disabled, so the class is not needed.

knownIssues.issue: The docs say to use role="switch", but none of the docs markup has it; they also advise aria-checked, which is redundant on a native checkbox.
knownIssues.fix: Add role="switch" to every docs example and drop the aria-checked advice.

knownIssues.issue: On can be shown two ways (native checked or gds-toggle--on), and they behave differently when disabled: with :checked the track stays primary (only dimmed) and still changes colour on hover; with --on alone it turns grey.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drive the look only from the native state, add .gds-toggle__input:disabled styles that win over :checked, and keep --on for docs previews.

knownIssues.issue: Disabled is class-only; a native disabled input without the class still looks enabled.
knownIssues.fix: v3: style from .gds-toggle__input:disabled ~ .gds-toggle__track.

knownIssues.issue: Only a native checkbox is supported. A <button aria-pressed> has no styles (the focus ring and on state need the input).
knownIssues.fix: Keep the checkbox pattern; if a button version is needed, add [aria-checked="true"] styles on the wrapper.

knownIssues.issue: The knob slide uses translateX, which goes the wrong way in right-to-left layouts.
knownIssues.fix: Use a logical property or flip the transform under [dir="rtl"].

contracts.name: Tooltip
contracts.summary: A small dark label that appears on hover or keyboard focus of a control, CSS only.
useWhen: Naming an icon-only button in a toolbar (Bold, Insert image, Preview).
A short, non-essential hint about what a control does ("Saves your draft locally").
Showing the keyboard shortcut of an action (Save · ⌘S).

dontUseWhen.case: Content with links or buttons, or anything people need to read carefully
Information needed to complete the task (format rules, errors)
A list of actions
Truncated table text that people need to read
dontUseWhen.use: wider column, wrapping, or a detail view

anatomy.description: Inline wrapper (position: relative, inline-flex) around the trigger and the bubble. The trigger is a focusable element (button, link) placed first; the bubble shows on :hover or :focus-within.
The label. Must be the last child of the wrapper. Dark surface, 12px text, no line wrap by default, arrow drawn with ::after. Above the trigger when no placement modifier is set.

attributes.id: Unique; referenced by aria-describedby on the trigger

anatomy.description: Keyboard shortcut chip after the label text (e.g. ⌘S).

modifiers.description: Above the trigger.
Below the trigger.
Left of the trigger.
Right of the trigger.
Max width 240px (short label).
Max width 290px (one sentence). Use with --multiline.
Max width 380px (two short sentences). Use with --multiline.
Lets text wrap at the max width (default is one line, no wrap).
Turns pointer events back on so links inside can be clicked. Avoid: see rules and known issues.

states.name: hidden
states.how: Default. opacity 0 + visibility hidden.

states.name: visible
states.how: Native :hover or :focus-within on .gds-tooltip, after --tooltip-delay-show (no delay with reduced motion).

states.name: forced open
states.how: Add is-open to .gds-tooltip (docs and JS-controlled tooltips). is-open is a shared global class, so it is not listed as a modifier here (see known issues).

a11y: Bubble: role="tooltip" and a unique id. Trigger: aria-describedby="<bubble id>".
The trigger must be focusable so keyboard users get the tooltip on focus (:focus-within).
An icon-only trigger needs its own aria-label; the tooltip describes, it does not name.
Never put the only copy of important information in a tooltip: touch screens have no hover.
The bubble ignores the pointer by default and closes when focus or pointer leaves; it cannot be dismissed with Escape (CSS only).

rules.rule: The bubble has role="tooltip" and an id; the trigger inside the same wrapper has aria-describedby with that id.
rules.why: Without the link, screen reader users never hear the tooltip.

rules.rule: The first child of .gds-tooltip is a focusable element (button, a[href], input).
rules.why: The bubble shows on :focus-within; a span or icon trigger never gets focus, so keyboard users never see it.

rules.rule: An icon-only trigger has its own aria-label, even with a tooltip.
rules.why: aria-describedby adds a description, not a name; the button would be announced as just "button".

rules.rule: The bubble is the last child of .gds-tooltip.
rules.why: The show selector uses the child combinator and the stacking assumes the bubble comes after the trigger.

rules.rule: No links or buttons inside the bubble; do not use --interactive. Use a popover for interactive content.
rules.why: role="tooltip" must not contain controls, and a hover-only surface is hard to reach with keyboard, touch and screen readers.
rules.removeInV3: Remove gds-tooltip__bubble--interactive.

rules.rule: Keep tooltip text to one short phrase. Longer text needs --multiline (and --md or --lg); more than two sentences belongs in a popover or on the page.
rules.why: Without --multiline the text does not wrap and runs past the bubble; long tooltips disappear before people finish reading.
rules.removeInV3: Wrap text by default so the size modifiers work without --multiline.

rules.rule: Tooltips hold only extra help. Labels, errors and rules people need go in visible text.
rules.why: Touch screens cannot hover, and the tooltip is hidden by default.

knownIssues.issue: WCAG 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus): the CSS-only bubble cannot be dismissed with Escape, and with pointer-events: none it closes when the pointer moves onto it.
knownIssues.fix: Add a tooltip mode to the ds-core controller (Escape to close, hoverable bubble), and keep the CSS version for simple labels.

knownIssues.issue: --interactive puts links inside an element with role="tooltip", which ARIA does not allow, and the docs show it as a supported pattern.
knownIssues.fix: Deprecate --interactive; point to popover.

knownIssues.issue: Placement is pure CSS: no flip near the viewport edges, only the width is clamped. Bubbles near the top or a scrolling container edge get cut off.
knownIssues.fix: Use createPopover() with role "tooltip" for flip / shift, or CSS anchor positioning later.

knownIssues.issue: The size modifiers only set max-width, but the default white-space: nowrap means they have no visible effect without --multiline.
knownIssues.fix: v3: wrap by default; drop --multiline.

knownIssues.issue: is-open (forced open) breaks the BEM naming rule and is also used by the table action-cell dropdown, so it cannot belong to one contract.
knownIssues.fix: v3: gds-tooltip--open.

knownIssues.issue: Placement uses physical left / right, so --left and --right do not flip in right-to-left layouts.
knownIssues.fix: Use logical properties (inset-inline-start / end) and name the modifiers --start / --end.
